arguments.prompt: Wide establishing shot of the square outside New Harnomy City Hall on a grey drizzling November morning. A heavy flat overcast, sheet-cake grey sky, no sun and no shadows; a light steady drizzle falls, fine rain visible against the dark stone, the granite paving wet with shallow puddles mirroring the grey sky; street lamps and windows glow warm and are doubled in the wet. The camera is locked off on a tripod and does not move at all: no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no drift, no handheld shake. Real-time speed, natural human movement, never slow motion. The only movement is small and human: a handful of pedestrians in winter coats walk slowly across the granite paving at a distance with their backs to the camera, a dog-walker crosses, a cyclist rolls slowly past under an umbrella, steam rises from the hot-food cart. The granite paving in front of the building's entrance steps stays open and empty throughout - nothing is built or stacked on it. The parked cars along the kerbs stay parked; the flatbed lumber truck and the white box van stand still with their engines off; the bus at the far corner pulls away slowly. On the far street beyond the square and along the side kerbs a few cars move slowly and steadily with their headlights and tail-lights on, reflected in the wet road, at an unhurried city pace - no car ever enters the square or comes near the stage. The damp mauve banner on the portico hangs heavy and barely stirs. Prestige political drama photographed on an Arri Alexa with anamorphic lenses: flat overcast daylight, slight 35mm film grain, colours desaturated about twelve percent, warm tungstens, deep browns and charcoals in the shadows, photographic realism.
